issues.item: Escape Route Planning: always plan an escape route before entering a place
issues.explanation: Escape route planning implies a prominent ongoing external-danger/triggered-threat pattern in public places, but the formulation specifies no active links involving Triggers or Threat, and the rest of the profile is centered on bodily vulnerability and negative beliefs rather than situational danger. This makes the item poorly aligned with the formulation and cross-node content.

issues.item: Distrust Others: People are not what they seem
issues.explanation: Distrust of others is not impossible after a life-threatening accident, but in this profile it introduces an interpersonal/paranoid theme that is not supported by the other selected items or the formulation. The remaining items focus on bodily unreliability and permanent damage after an accident, so this item is the least coherent with the trauma-linked appraisal pattern presented.

vignette: Amir's hands, once deft and sure, now trembled as he worked on his latest sculpture. It had been three years since the accident in his studio, when a falling block of marble crushed his leg, pinning him beneath its weight. The pain was still a vivid memory, but it was no longer just the physical ache that troubled him - it was the unshakeable feeling that his body had betrayed him. As he worked, Amir couldn't help but think about why this had happened to him. Was it a punishment for some past mistake? Had he been too confident in his abilities? The questions swirled in his mind like the dust motes dancing in the studio's dim light. He would often find himself lost in thought, replaying the accident over and over, searching for answers that never seemed to come. But Amir's introspection wasn't limited to philosophical musings. He had developed a constant vigilance, always on the lookout for signs of danger or injury. His eyes would scan his body, checking for any unusual sensations, no matter how minor. A twinge in his leg, a prickling sensation in his fingers - all were potential warnings that something was amiss. He would catch himself wincing at every little creak and groan of the old studio building, as if it too might be harboring secrets that could harm him. Physical exertion had become anathema to Amir. He avoided situations that put his body under stress, fearful that he might exacerbate the damage already done. His sculpture work, once a source of joy and expression, now felt like a perilous endeavor. He would hesitate before lifting heavy blocks or tools, his mind racing with worst-case scenarios. The studio, once his sanctuary, had become a minefield of potential threats. Amir's fear was not just about the physical consequences; it was also about what this accident had done to him as a person. He felt like he had been permanently changed for the worse - that some fundamental aspect of himself had been altered by the trauma. His body, once a trusted ally, now seemed fragile and unreliable. The weight of this realization hung over him like a shadow, coloring every waking moment. As the months went by, Amir's avoidance behaviors began to take their toll. He stopped taking on new commissions, fearful of not being able to deliver due to his physical limitations. His relationships with friends and family suffered as he became increasingly withdrawn, unable to shake off the feeling that he was no longer the person they once knew. It wasn't until his granddaughter, Sophia, came to visit from out of town that Amir realized just how isolated he had become. She had always loved watching him work in the studio, mesmerized by the way his hands could coax beauty from raw stone. But now, as she looked around at the dust-covered tools and half-finished projects, her eyes filled with concern. "Jiddo," she asked, using the affectionate Arabic term for grandfather, "what's happened to your studio?" Amir was taken aback by the question. He had been so caught up in his own fears and doubts that he hadn't noticed how much of himself he had lost. It was then that he knew he needed help - not just to reclaim his physical strength but also to rediscover the sense of purpose and confidence that had once defined him. As Amir sat in his dimly lit studio, surrounded by the remnants of a life on hold, he felt a glimmer of determination. He would seek out therapy, and slowly begin to rebuild the shattered trust between himself and his own body. It wouldn't be easy, but with Sophia's words echoing in his mind, he knew it was time to take the first step towards healing.
